//: Bundled plugins this build ships but must not start by themselves. Ids listed here are stamped with "enabledByDefault": false in the manifest scripts/sync-bundled-plugins.mjs expands into apps/desktop/resources/plugins. Host-core creates the row from that flag on first boot and, on every later launch, keeps whatever the user chose (crates/host-core/src/plugins/registry.rs), so this file decides only the state of a machine that has never seen the plugin.
//community.workbuddy-connect: Retired into the app (ADR 0397): the in-app provider gateway runs this bridge, and the plugin itself is now listed in bundled-plugins-excluded.json so it cannot ship. An entry here would only matter for a machine that still has the plugin installed, which the exclusion takes care of.
//defaultDisabledOnPlatforms: Ids that ship switched off on one platform only. A plugin whose implementation cannot run on a platform must not arrive enabled there: it lists as a working tool, opens an empty panel and reports nothing, which is worse than not offering it. `local.terminal` drives the shell through embedded Python `pty`/`fcntl`/`termios`/`pwd` modules and defaults to `/bin/zsh`, so it only runs on macOS.
//local.pi-bot: Starts switched off on Windows because of what it starts when it loads, not because it is unwanted: `onStartup` loads it on every launch, it registers a resident background service and a local MCP listener, and its Windows voice path is a hidden PowerShell/.NET recorder. A behaviour-based endpoint engine reads that combination - unsigned host, resident service, hidden interpreter holding the microphone - as remote-access tooling, which is how this deployment's KES quarantined the app. It stays bundled and a user can switch it on; this file only decides the state of a machine that has never seen it.
